"""Module 25 exercises. pytest 25_security All defensive. Each function is a control you'd actually put between untrusted input and a dangerous operation. Two habits the tests enforce throughout: - compare secrets with `secrets.compare_digest`, never `==` - fail CLOSED — when in doubt, reject """ from __future__ import annotations from typing import Any def hash_password(password: str, *, n: int = 2**14) -> str: """Hash a password for storage, self-describing so the cost can be raised later. Return a single string in this exact format (the fields joined by "$"): scrypt$$$

$$ - Use `hashlib.scrypt` with `r=8`, `p=1`, `dklen=32`, and a FRESH `secrets.token_bytes(16)` salt on every call. - Two calls with the same password must produce different strings (different salts). - An empty password raises ValueError. Storing the parameters alongside the hash is what lets you migrate to a higher cost later without locking every user out. """ raise NotImplementedError def verify_password(stored: str, password: str) -> bool: """Check a password against a `hash_password` string. Never raises on bad input. - Recompute with the parameters parsed OUT of `stored` — that's the whole reason they're in there. - Compare with `secrets.compare_digest`, not `==`. - A malformed, empty or unknown-algorithm `stored` value returns False rather than raising. Fail closed: an exception here becomes a 500, and a 500 on the login path is a much more interesting signal to an attacker than "no". """ raise NotImplementedError def generate_token(n_bytes: int = 32) -> str: """Return a URL-safe random token from a CSPRNG. - Use `secrets.token_urlsafe` — NOT `random`, which is a predictable PRNG. - `n_bytes < 16` raises ValueError (anything shorter is brute-forceable). - Tokens must be unique across calls; the tests generate 10,000 and check. """ raise NotImplementedError def sign_payload(secret: bytes, body: bytes, timestamp: int) -> str: """Return the hex HMAC-SHA256 of `f"{timestamp}.".encode() + body`. Signing the timestamp TOGETHER WITH the body is what makes replay detection possible; signing the body alone lets a captured request be resent forever. """ raise NotImplementedError def verify_payload( secret: bytes, body: bytes, timestamp: int, signature: str, *, max_age: int = 300, now: float | None = None ) -> bool: """Verify a webhook signature. Returns a bool; never raises. - Recompute and compare with `hmac.compare_digest`. - Reject when `abs(now - timestamp) > max_age` (replay protection), where `now` defaults to `time.time()` — injected so the tests are deterministic (module 09). - Reject a tampered body, a wrong secret, a malformed signature, and a future timestamp beyond the window. - Do the cheap timestamp check first, but do NOT skip the signature check because of it — both must pass. """ raise NotImplementedError def sanitize_filename(name: str, *, max_length: int = 255) -> str: """Reduce a user-supplied filename to something safe to write to disk. - Keep only the BASENAME: "../../etc/passwd" -> "passwd", "C:\\\\windows\\\\x" -> "x" (handle both separators; the client OS is not your OS). - Allow only `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`; replace every other character with "_". - Collapse runs of "." so ".." can't survive, and strip leading dots (no hidden files, no traversal). - Truncate to `max_length`, preserving the extension if there is one. - If nothing usable remains, return "unnamed". - Reject Windows reserved device names (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-9, LPT1-9, case-insensitively, with or without an extension) by prefixing with "_". This is a defence in DEPTH, not the primary one: you still write into a directory you control and check with `safe_join` (module 19). Two independent controls. """ raise NotImplementedError def is_safe_url(url: str, allowed_hosts: frozenset[str] | None = None) -> bool: """Decide whether a user-supplied URL is safe to fetch or redirect to. Reject (return False) when: - the scheme is not http or https (blocks `javascript:`, `data:`, `file:`) - there is no hostname - the host is a literal IP that is loopback, private, link-local, reserved or unspecified — 127.0.0.1, 10.x, 192.168.x, 172.16-31.x, and especially 169.254.169.254, the cloud metadata endpoint - the hostname is "localhost" or ends in ".localhost" / ".internal" / ".local" - `allowed_hosts` is given and the hostname is not in it (exact match, lowercased) - the URL contains credentials (`user:pass@host`) or a newline (header injection) Accept otherwise. This one function is both the SSRF guard and the open-redirect guard; they're the same check with a different allow-list. """ raise NotImplementedError def redact(data: Any, *, extra_keys: frozenset[str] = frozenset()) -> Any: """Recursively redact secrets in a nested structure, for safe logging. - A dict key is sensitive when its lowercased name CONTAINS any of: password, passwd, secret, token, api_key, apikey, authorization, auth, credential, private_key, session, cookie — plus anything in `extra_keys`. - A sensitive value becomes the string "[REDACTED]", whatever its type. - Recurse into nested dicts, lists and tuples (preserving the container type). - Non-sensitive scalars pass through untouched. - The INPUT MUST NOT BE MODIFIED — return a new structure. - Handle self-referencing structures without infinite recursion (track ids seen). Redacting centrally, in one function used by your log formatter, is what stops the one call site you forgot from leaking a token. """ raise NotImplementedError def parse_json_safely(text: str, *, max_bytes: int = 1_000_000, max_depth: int = 20) -> Any: """Parse untrusted JSON with hard limits, so a hostile document can't take you down. - Reject input longer than `max_bytes` (measured in UTF-8 bytes) -> ValueError. - Reject nesting deeper than `max_depth` -> ValueError. A 10,000-deep document will otherwise blow the recursion limit inside the parser, and `RecursionError` is not something your request handler is ready for. - Invalid JSON -> ValueError (not `json.JSONDecodeError` leaking out; wrap it). - Never use `eval` or `pickle` for this. Ever. Check the depth on the PARSED object rather than by counting brackets in the text — escaped brackets inside strings would fool a textual count. """ raise NotImplementedError
